entry.title: Puron is now in the COSMIC Store!
entry.summary: Puron is approved for the COSMIC Flatpak repository, so it can be installed from the COSMIC Store.
entry.content:
Puron is now in the COSMIC Flatpak repository. System76 reviewed the package and approved it.

The COSMIC Flatpak repository is where System76 publishes applets and other Flatpaks for COSMIC that are not suitable for Flathub. The COSMIC Store reads it. For Puron, this means:

  • Puron shows in the COSMIC Store with the other applets, and can be installed from there. A download of the .deb or a build from source is no longer necessary.
  • Updates come through the store. A new release of Puron shows there when the repository has taken it in.
  • The repository builds Puron from a public manifest, for x86_64 and for aarch64. The .deb is for x86_64 only.

The Flatpak has version 1.7.0. It reads the same sensors as the .deb, except liquidctl devices. The two packages share their settings, so a move from one to the other keeps every setting and every pinned reading.

The pull request is pop-os/cosmic-flatpak#421.

entry.title: puron 1.7.0
entry.summary: Each temperature in the popup is colored by how hot it runs, and the readings have the look of the Settings and About pages.
entry.content:
Each temperature in the popup is colored by how hot it runs, and the readings have the look of the Settings and About pages.

Changes:

  • added: Each temperature in the popup is colored by how hot it runs: in the normal text color while it is cool, in the theme's warning color when it runs warm, and in the theme's red when it runs hot. The limits suit each kind of device, so a CPU or a graphics card may run warmer than a drive before it changes color, and a temperature has the same color whether it is shown in Celsius or in Fahrenheit. Only the value is colored, never the name; fan, voltage and power readings keep the normal text color.
  • added: Each device name in the popup has the icon of its kind of device beside it, such as the CPU, the graphics card, a drive, the Wi-Fi card, a wired network card or a memory module, in that kind's color.
  • changed: The readings in the popup now have the look of the Settings and About pages, in the desktop theme's colors, so that a light and a dark theme both work. Each section heading has a small colored tile with the section's icon. Each device's readings sit in a rounded card with a thin divider between two readings, and the fan, voltage and power readings of a section share one card. The readings, their order, their texts and what a click does stay the same, and so does the panel.
  • changed: The check mark of a pinned reading is in the theme's accent color, and "Settings" and "About" each have a small icon beside their text.
  • changed: On the Settings page, the tile of the section "Generic Sensor Providers" now has the same color as the Temperature tile in the popup.
  • changed: On the Settings page, a long label or state line under a sensor provider's switch now wraps instead of squeezing the switch.

Source: https://github.com/elalonde/puron/releases/tag/v1.7.0

entry.title: jig 0.9.1
entry.summary: Fixes for the trust marks and for "jig report" of 0.9.0, and "jig tag" accepts a review loop that a fix unit closed.
entry.content:
Fixes for the trust marks and for "jig report" of 0.9.0, and "jig tag" accepts a review loop that a fix unit closed.

Changes:

  • added: "jig tag" accepts a closed review loop whose must-fix findings a fix unit applied, with no second review: a row of the table "Closed review loops" may have a fourth cell, the ID of the fix unit.
  • changed: "jig run-check", at the time cap or a stop signal, sends SIGTERM to the process group of the command and waits up to 30 seconds before SIGKILL, so that a cleanup can finish.
  • changed: "jig batch" stops with exit 15 on a must-fix or should-fix finding that it cannot count, and names its line.
  • changed: The templates of "jig new" show each celebration at the top of the reply to the owner's next message, and not before.
  • fixed: "jig start" and "jig orch" set all the trust marks of a start with one read and one rename of the state file of Claude Code. A write of a session in between is no longer lost.
  • fixed: A folder that the list of a start holds twice gets its trust mark. In 0.9.0 it got no mark, and its session waited at the trust dialog.
  • fixed: "jig report", for a product that has no branch of the conf's name yet, reads every origin branch also for the vector checks. In 0.9.0 only the check of the commits of the unit did so.
  • fixed: The stall check of "jig orch" reads the activity files of the other project in the home of the orchestrator account that the conf file names.

Source: https://github.com/elalonde/jig/releases/tag/v0.9.1

entry.content:
The first release of the line 0.9: jig answers the folder trust dialog of Claude Code before a session starts, and a project can give its sessions more folders.

Changes:

  • added: jig marks each folder of a session as trusted in the state file of Claude Code before the session starts, also each folder that the session gets with "--add-dir". Before, a session that jig started could wait at the trust dialog with nobody to answer it. "jig start", "jig orch" and "jig new" each print a line "trust ACCOUNT: VALUE".
  • added: A project can give the sessions of an account more folders in a section "## Directories" of its kickoff record. "jig start" passes them with "--add-dir" and refuses a folder that is not in the approved list of the account.
  • changed: The supervisor "jig orch" no longer appends the event "hourly update". An hour with no change still gets its "idle:" line in the updates log of the project.
  • changed: The supervisor reads "BRANCH" of the conf file at each report poll. After a move to a new version line it fetches the new line and announces only the reports of that line.
  • changed: "jig report" accepts a product commit that any origin branch of the product holds when the product has no branch of the conf's name yet.
  • changed: "jig validate prompt" refuses a ROLE section that splits "Spec tag:" over two lines.
  • changed: The orchestrator templates of "jig new" roll over only when "jig ctx" says so, never at a batch boundary, and upgrade jig at each batch boundary.

entry.title: jig 0.8.0
entry.summary: The first release of the line 0.8: an orchestrator can say that it waits on another project and learns when that project stalls, "jig new" takes a product that already exists, and the trace reads Rust and C.
entry.content:
The first release of the line 0.8: an orchestrator can say that it waits on another project and learns when that project stalls, "jig new" takes a product that already exists, and the trace reads Rust and C.

Changes:

  • added: The supervisor "jig orch" writes the activity of its project to a file once a minute: "unit", "busy", "idle" or "down". "jig orch PROJECT status" prints it.
  • added: "jig orch PROJECT wait-on OTHER WHAT" records that the orchestrator waits on another project of the host. When that project has been idle or down for the stall time, 15 minutes unless the host config sets "ORCH_STALL_MINUTES", the supervisor writes a "stall" event, and a "resumed" event when the project works again.
  • added: "jig orch PROJECT rollover" lets the orchestrator session end itself, so that the supervisor starts the next session. Before, a person had to type "/exit".
  • added: "jig new PROJECT --existing" sets up a project whose product repository already exists on GitHub. It writes no file into the product.
  • added: "jig trace gen" and lint A read the comments of Rust files and of C files and headers. "jig trace form" names the Rust method or the C function that a change falls in.
  • added: "jig start" accepts a kickoff tag on the ROLE line of an implementer unit while origin holds no spec tag, so a project can run implementer units between its kickoff and its first spec tag.
  • added: The "CLAUDE.md" that "jig new" writes has a new section, "Commit message standard". "jig start" refuses an implementer prompt whose ROLE line does not name it and "Comment standard".
  • changed: "jig trace gen" reads "specs/id-map.tsv", as "jig trace check" does: an old ID in a comment is written into the trace as the new IDs of its row.
  • changed: The orchestrator template starts a batch detached, so that a rollover leaves it running, and has a new section, "Waiting on another project".
  • fixed: When the supervisor loop ends, it looks for forks of its last session at once and again a fork window later (60 seconds unless set), also at a stop. Before, a fork that showed up after a stop was never ended, and the next start ran a second orchestrator beside it. A stop therefore now takes at least the fork window.
  • fixed: The tests of the orchestrator loop, the release and the status line no longer depend on wall-clock margins.

Source: https://github.com/elalonde/jig/releases/tag/v0.8.0

entry.title: jig 0.7.0
entry.summary: The first release of the line 0.7: heavy checks share a limited number of slots on the host, and a running unit can get a new expected time.
entry.content:
The first release of the line 0.7: heavy checks share a limited number of slots on the host, and a running unit can get a new expected time.

Changes:

  • added: A row of "checks.tsv" may have a fifth column, its weight, "heavy" or "light". The host config may set "HEAVY_SLOTS", the number of heavy rows that may run at once on the host. A heavy row in "jig run-check" waits for a free slot, and the wait does not count toward the time cap of the row.
  • added: "jig wait PROJECT ID --expected MINUTES" gives a running unit a new expected time. Every wait that already runs, and a running "jig batch", follow the new value.
  • changed: "jig start" sets "core.hooksPath" of a product clone to "hooks" when the product tracks files in "hooks/" and no git config sets the value yet. It leaves alone a pre-commit hook that the product tracks.
  • changed: The product clone inside the "-dev" clone, the place of the releases before 0.6, is no longer found by any tool.
  • changed: "jig run-check" handles SIGTERM, SIGHUP and SIGINT: it ends the whole process group of the command, frees its slot and exits 128 plus the signal number.
  • changed: "jig release prepare" reads every row of "checks.tsv" with the same reader as "jig run-check". A bad time cap on a row of any account now refuses.
  • changed: "jig new" says how to recover when it refuses a product clone with no "-dev" clone beside it.

Source: https://github.com/elalonde/jig/releases/tag/v0.7.0

entry.title: jig 0.5.0
entry.summary: The first release of the line 0.5: the term check runs before every commit, the supervisor writes its events to a file, and the status line of Claude Code is part of jig.
entry.content:
The first release of the line 0.5: the term check runs before every commit, the supervisor writes its events to a file, and the status line of Claude Code is part of jig.

Changes:

  • added: A pre-commit hook runs the term check before each commit in a product clone. It refuses the commit when the check fails, runs out of time or is missing. "jig start" and "jig new" install the hook.
  • added: "jig orch PROJECT events" prints the events of the supervisor as they come. With "--old" it prints the events of the session before.
  • added: "jig-statusline", the status line of Claude Code. It shows the user, role, branch, model and effort, then the run time, the 5-hour and weekly use, the health note of the host and the model policy warning.
  • added: "jig tag" and "jig start" take the approval tags of the product stage, "spec-X.Y" and "spec-X.YrM".
  • changed: The supervisor "jig orch" no longer types into the session of the orchestrator. It appends each event to the file "events.log", once and in order.
  • changed: "jig new" sets the status line in the Claude Code settings of each account to "jig-statusline".
  • changed: "MODEL_POLICY" now comes only from the host config and has no default. "jig new" refuses a host config without it.
  • changed: "jig trace check" no longer asks for the ledger entry of a release commit, so the check passes inside "jig release prepare".
  • changed: The tools of jig no longer ship message-of-the-day lines.
  • fixed: An inbox file is recorded as announced only after its line is written. A stop between the two now announces the file once at the next start.
  • fixed: "jig start" refuses a hook path outside the product clone.
  • fixed: The status line treats a reset time that is not a valid clock time as unknown.
  • fixed: A tag such as "spec-1.2.3" is no longer read as "spec-1.2".

Source: https://github.com/elalonde/jig/releases/tag/v0.5.0

entry.title: jig 0.4.0
entry.summary: The first public release: jig now makes its own releases and the releases of the projects that it builds.
entry.content:
The first public release: jig now makes its own releases and the releases of the projects that it builds.

Changes:

  • added: "jig release" prepares a release, publishes it and compares the published files with the staged ones. It waits for green CI and proves the release commit from a clean clone with an offline build of the source archive.
  • added: "jig terms check" looks for private terms in the product, its commit messages and its built files. "jig privacy scan" looks for serials, host names, addresses, UUIDs and MAC addresses in fixtures and captures.
  • added: "jig upgrade" downloads a release, checks it against its SHA256SUMS and installs it. "jig changelog --since" prints the entries after a version.
  • added: The make targets "version-bump", "package", "package-check" and "source-archive" for the product.
  • added: "jig new" gives a new product a CI workflow that runs "make check" on every push.

Source: https://github.com/elalonde/jig/releases/tag/v0.4.0

entry.title: puron 1.1.0
entry.summary: The popup shows every reading at once, grouped by device, and a click on a line puts it on the panel.
entry.content:
The popup shows every reading at once, grouped by device, and a click on a line puts it on the panel.

Changes:

  • changed: The popup shows everything at once, in the sections Temperature, Fan, Voltage and Power. Nothing opens or closes any more, so the arrows and the "Group Items" settings are gone.
  • changed: Temperatures are listed by device: the CPU first, with every CPU reading under it, then GPUs, drives and other chips, each under its name, or the label you set in lm-sensors on a drive's "Composite" sensor.
  • changed: A device with several readings also has a "Maximum" line, the highest of them at each poll, and marks one line "(default)": the CPU's package reading, a drive's composite reading, otherwise the first.
  • changed: A click on a line checks it, and a checked line shows on the panel; several can be checked, and the panel shows them in popup order. A new install checks each "(default)" line. The Maximum that version 1.0.0 pinned moves to the CPU's default line, once.
  • changed: With lm-sensors and the "nvme-cli" switch both on, a drive no longer shows the same reading twice: the lm-sensors line stays, and a pin on the other one moves to it.
  • changed: The check mark is a small fixed size with a gap before the text, and section headings are drawn stronger.
  • changed: Every line stays on one line. The popup grows to fit, and text over 44 characters is shortened with "…". A popup taller than its limit scrolls.

Source: https://github.com/elalonde/puron/releases/tag/v1.1.0

entry.title: The jig spec is accepted
entry.summary: jig is my build system for software that agents write.
entry.content:
jig is my build system for software that agents write. Each project has an orchestrator, a spec writer and an implementer.

The first spec had four review rounds. I judged it overengineered and had it written again from the start. The accepted spec has 14 sections and no decision log.

Each role is a separate Unix account. I talk to one orchestrator for each project, and each orchestrator has its own tmux session.

The shared tools are in one repository with versions. A project upgrades when it is convenient, at the end of a batch of work.

I want jig to stay light. It is a build system and nothing more.

entry.title: eos defines and loads its own GDT
entry.summary: eos no longer runs on the segments that GRUB leaves behind: it defines its own GDT and loads it at boot.
entry.content:
eos no longer runs on the segments that GRUB leaves behind. The kernel now defines its own GDT and loads it at boot.

The table has three entries: the null descriptor, a code segment and a data segment. Both segments are flat: base 0, with a limit of 4 GB.

The loader disables interrupts, runs lgdt, and loads the data selector into ds, es, fs, gs and ss. It sets the stack pointer directly after ss. A far jump then loads the code selector into cs.

The commit is df92949.
